_about: Canonical question bank for the DayNova Individual AI Assessment. Part 1 (SCARF) and the driver write-ups come from the DayNova Diagnostic. Part 2 (AI habits) is scored 0-3 per question, 2 questions per NOVA pillar. scripts/build_report.py reads this file, so edit questions here and nowhere else.

scarf.instructions: Rank all five from most important to you (1st) to least important (5th). There are no right answers. Your honest ranking is the data.

questions.stem: When your organization announces a major AI initiative, your concern is most likely:

options.status: Whether your expertise will still be valued
options.certainty: Whether you will know what is expected of you
options.autonomy: Whether you will have a say in how AI gets used in your own work
options.relatedness: Whether your team will still feel connected through the change
options.fairness: Whether the rollout will be applied evenly across the organization

questions.stem: You feel most resistant to a new AI tool when:

options.status: You are treated as a beginner in front of peers who have used it longer
options.certainty: The instructions keep changing or feel vague
options.autonomy: You are forced to use it in a specific way
options.relatedness: You cannot get help from anyone you trust
options.fairness: Other teams are getting better support or training than yours

questions.stem: In a successful AI transformation, what would matter most to you?

options.status: Being recognized as someone who adapted well
options.certainty: Having clarity on the new way of working
options.autonomy: Maintaining control over how you do your job
options.relatedness: Going through it together with your team
options.fairness: Knowing the process was fair to everyone involved

questions.stem: You are most likely to disengage from an AI rollout when:

options.status: You feel your contributions go unnoticed
options.certainty: Plans keep shifting and you cannot predict next week
options.autonomy: Decisions are made about your work without your input
options.relatedness: You feel isolated from the people you usually work with
options.fairness: You see favoritism in who gets opportunities

questions.stem: After an AI initiative is complete, you would feel it was worthwhile if:

options.autonomy: You gained more control over your work
options.relatedness: Your relationships with colleagues got stronger

habits.instructions: Pick the answer closest to how you work today, not how you'd like to work.

questions.stem: How clear are you on which parts of your job AI should help with?
options: I haven't figured that out yet
I have a general sense, but nothing specific
I know a few specific tasks where it helps
I have a clear list of where AI helps in my role, and where it doesn't belong

questions.stem: When AI gives you a weak answer, what do you usually do?
options: Give up and do it myself
Rephrase the question and try again
Add context, examples, or constraints until it's right
I've set up reusable instructions, projects, or prompts so it starts with the right context

questions.stem: How often do you use AI tools in your work?
options: Rarely or never
A few times a month
A few times a week
Daily. It's part of how I work

questions.stem: Which best describes how you use AI?
options: I haven't found a regular use yet
Quick questions, lookups, or rewording
Drafting, summarizing, or analyzing real work
Multi-step workflows, custom assistants, or automations I've set up

questions.stem: Before you use AI output in real work, what do you do?
options: I mostly use it as-is, or I don't use AI output yet
I skim it for anything obviously wrong
I fact-check the key points and edit it into my own voice
I check it against a clear standard for what good looks like, and I know where AI tends to slip in my work

questions.stem: How confident are you at spotting when AI gets something wrong (a factual error, an off tone, a flawed recommendation)?
options: Not confident yet
I catch the obvious mistakes
I usually catch it
Very confident. I know its typical failure points in my field

questions.stem: In a typical week, how much time does AI save you?
options: None yet, or I'm not sure
Less than an hour
One to three hours
More than three hours

questions.stem: What happens with the time AI saves you?
options: It hasn't saved me time yet, or I haven't noticed
It gets absorbed by more of the same work
Some of it goes to higher-value work
I deliberately put it into strategic, creative, or growth work

blocker.stem: What would most help you get more out of AI right now?

options.start: Knowing where to start in my own role
options.permission: Clarity on what I'm allowed to use and share
options.trust: Being able to trust the outputs
options.time: Time set aside to learn and experiment
options.fit: Tools that fit the way my work is actually done
options.next: Nothing's in the way. I want to go further and build more advanced workflows
